part15_cutover_configuration_design.production_cold_root_at_runtime: resolve_cold_root() reads a new TRANSFER_COLD_ROOT env var, falling back to database/cold_segments (a production-parallel path, distinct from the candidate's database/_p5a_migration_build/cold_segments/ used only for R2's own qualification runs via the override parameter).
part15_cutover_configuration_design.registry_init_timing_as_actually_built: Lazy, first-request/first-call init via the module-level _factory singleton in get_transfer_reader() -- NOT a Gunicorn post_fork hook. This works correctly today because config/gunicorn.conf.py runs workers=1 (single process, 24 threads), so there is only ever one process-level singleton to initialize, and the first thread to call get_transfer_reader() pays the one-time connection-open cost (measured: the 42+1 connections open in well under a second based on the fd-count proof in Part 2-4). If a future config change moves to workers>1, a post_fork hook in config/gunicorn.conf.py calling get_transfer_reader() eagerly (or reset_transfer_reader_factory() + a warm-up call) would be the correct extension point to avoid a per-worker cold-start penalty on that worker's first real request -- documented here as the forward-looking design note, not implemented (no such hook exists in the current gunicorn.conf.py and none was added, since workers=1 makes it unnecessary today).
part15_cutover_configuration_design.hot_cold_never_activate_separately: get_transfer_reader(fail_closed=True) (the default, and the only mode any adapter added in this milestone uses) raises ColdRegistryUnavailableError if zero COLD segments qualify -- a HISTORICAL_HOT_COLD_REQUIRED consumer therefore cannot silently start serving HOT-only results the moment HOT activates before COLD is ready. This makes the COLD registry a hard prerequisite of reader usability by construction, not by caller discipline.
part15_cutover_configuration_design.other_historical_consumer_init: Each adapter function (get_funders_via_hot_cold, _compute_wallet_age_via_hot_cold, _transfer_graph_stats_totals_via_hot_cold, funding_signature_for_quick_launch_via_hot_cold) takes `reader` as a parameter rather than constructing its own -- callers are expected to obtain one reader per request (or reuse a longer-lived one) via cold_segment_registry.get_transfer_reader(), so there is exactly one connection-management pattern for the whole codebase to reason about.
